claim: At N=64 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, e<=0.5), the final layer-1 force margin is 0.247 for seed 22 (R2 0.697 vs control 0.450, spread 0.003) and 0.234 for seed 23 (R2 0.684 vs control 0.450, spread 0.041). Both are >= 0.23, which puts N=64 at the N=16 level (0.236-0.275) and far above N=256 (0.033-0.040). With seeds 20/21 (0.215/0.261), the four N=64 seeds average about 0.239, so the force collapse lies between N=64 and N=256 rather than declining gradually. The flat-accel_step part of the hypothesis held: the layer-4 accel_step margin is 0.207 for seed 22 (R2 0.902 vs control 0.694) and 0.186 for seed 23 (R2 0.922 vs control 0.736). Headroom-normalized, that is 0.68 and 0.70, inside the predicted [0.62, 0.77] band and matching N=16 (0.68-0.69). Force leads accel_step on raw margin but trails it on normalized margin (0.45/0.43).
confidence_note: Both runs completed all 3000 steps, and both seeds meet the pre-registered expected-if-false force criterion, so seeds agree. Several things limit the result. (1) Seed 23 clears the 0.23 cut by only 0.004, and its force control spread (0.041) is the largest in this experiment. (2) Force is still rising at step 3000 in both seeds (about +0.009 to +0.012 per 500 steps), while accel_step has levelled off. The 'step vs gradual' reading therefore depends on comparing all N at a fixed 3000 steps, and growth rates could still differ by N. (3) Force peaks at layer 1, the same layer as distance (margin 0.70-0.71), so the force margin may be a nonlinear read of distance rather than an m2-weighted force code; no residualized probe exists yet. (4) Everything uses data_seed 0. (5) The 'refuted' verdict applies to the primary force prediction (gradual decline); the secondary flat-normalized-accel_step prediction was supported. The verdict would change if an N=128 arm landed midway (about 0.10-0.15), which would make the decline look gradual in log N, or if longer training let N=256 force catch up.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-024830-7d2f (issue 0): Accepted. The pre-registered expected_if_false (force >= 0.23 in both N=64 seeds) shows only that N=64 is not below the N=16 level (0.236-0.275). With just N=16, 64 and 256 available, it cannot tell a step between N=64 and N=256 apart from a gradual decline above N=64. The finding's own confidence note gave N=128 at about 0.10-0.15 as the condition that would change that reading. f-20261013-015951-62c7 then measured N=128 at 0.150 and 0.131. I withdraw the step interpretation. The refutation covers only the clause 'N=64 force sits between N=16 and N=256 (<= 0.22)', which fails in both seeds (0.247 and 0.234). The current best description, at a fixed 3000 steps, is: force is flat from N=16 to N=64, then falls by about 0.1 per doubling of N (N=128: 0.13-0.15; N=256: 0.03-0.04). That is gradual in log N above N=64, not a step. Even that picture depends on training length. At 6000 steps N=128 reached 0.163-0.178 and N=256 reached 0.044-0.139, both still rising. This cycle's 12000-step N=128 and N=256 arms test whether the decline is slower growth or a lower ceiling. Status stays replicated, because both seeds independently meet the pre-registered refutation clause.

Response to review r-20261013-024830-7d2f (issue 0): Accepted. The pre-registered expected_if_false (force >= 0.23 in both N=64 seeds) shows only that N=64 is not below N=16: force is roughly flat from N=16 (0.236-0.275) to N=64 (0.215-0.261, four seeds). It cannot separate 'a step between N=64 and N=256' from 'a gradual decline'. f-20261013-015951-62c7 then found N=128 force margins of 0.150 and 0.131, between N=64 and N=256. That is exactly the case this finding's confidence note said would undercut the step reading. I withdraw the step interpretation. The refutation stands only in its narrow form: force does not decline gradually across N=16 to N=64. The correct description of the full curve is flat from N=16 to N=64, then a decline of roughly 0.1 per doubling from N=64 to N=256, measured at 3000 steps. The 6000-step runs show force still rising at both N=128 and N=256, so even that shape may reflect growth rate rather than final level. This cycle's 12000-step N=128 and N=256 arms test that directly. The status stays as is, because the narrow pre-registered criterion was met in both seeds.
